title: Folded Space
thesis: At level 10 the visitor's own drawing goes into a real ReLU network running in their tab, and the lab shows what no sampled picture can: the exact flat-walled cells around the drawing, each one certified, with their count; the one picture the network applies inside the drawing's cell, which is also the attack; the corner of the cube of small changes that flips the answer, called by the visitor before the engine steps it; and a network the visitor hardens on their own corners until its walls move and that picture turns toward the strokes of the rival digit. Every claim is judged by exact geometry and by measured numbers set beside published results (Montufar et al., NeurIPS 2014; Hanin and Rolnick, ICML 2019; Goodfellow, Shlens and Szegedy, ICLR 2015; Tsipras et al., ICLR 2019), the visitor keeps their drawings, calls and flip ledger, and the page says plainly that exact cells belong to ReLU networks and blur into bands under smooth activations.
bindings_ref: The bindings (canon, 12 units fs-u1 to fs-u12, 19 fiction entries fs-f1 to fs-f19, 5 known setup failures fs-k1 to fs-k5) are declared in the lab's private plan (its bindings.json of 2026-11-21). Each axis lists the units and fiction entries its rungs test; rung 5 of each axis is its share of the fiction inventory at the depicted detail.

axes.name: Exactness of the cell geometry
axes.metric: Certificate failures per slice (target 0); the relative error of the cells' summed area against the slice's square; agreement of the first layer's count with the line-arrangement formula; the share of shared edges whose two cells differ in exactly one neuron (target 100%); the dimensions of slice computed exactly (segment, plane, 3-flat); and from rung 7 the census's agreement with published region counts.
axes.how_checked: Run node tools/lab_tests.mjs dimensions and read the tests of the mosaic; open the page on every example and on 3 drawings of your own and read the count and the certificate line; read the mosaic module for any sampled grid on the path to the drawn cells; from rung 7 run the committed census script and open each cited paper at the figure or theorem the page names.
ladder: No cell is computed: the page shows the network's answer alone, or nothing.
At least sampled cells: points on a grid of a plane are coloured by their activation pattern or their answer, the method of TensorFlow Playground.

Exact cells on a segment: a segment between two inputs (two drawings, or a drawing and a stepped copy of it) is split at every point where a hidden neuron's pre-activation changes sign, found exactly (by solving each neuron's affine pre-activation along the segment, or by clipping the segment to exactly computed convex cells) with no sampling along it, and the number of walls crossed is printed.

Exact cells on a plane through three inputs: the square around them is subdivided neuron by neuron and layer by layer into convex polygons (Hanin and Rolnick, ICML 2019), every hidden layer is cut, the integer count of cells is printed, and no sampled grid lies on the path from the network to the drawn cells.

The mosaic proves itself: on every plane the page draws, a vertex certificate (each neuron's pre-activation has its cell's sign at every vertex of the cell) runs and its result is printed on the page beside the count, and a node test on at least 6 planes asserts 0 certificate failures, cell areas summing to the square within 1e-9 relative, unique activation patterns, and a first-layer count equal to 1 plus the walls crossing the square plus their crossings inside it.

Fiction made real (fs-f3, fs-f16, fs-f17): the plane runs through any three drawings the visitor chooses, their own or the examples; a node test asserts that every two cells sharing an edge of positive length differ in exactly one neuron, the one whose wall it is; the census prints the count per slice, per layer and per training step beside the published bounds for the network's sizes with the slice's dimension as the input dimension (the upper bound of Serra, Tjandraatmadja and Ramalingam, ICML 2018; the lower bound on the maximum of Montufar et al., NeurIPS 2014; each formula on the page) and the published observation (Hanin and Rolnick, ICML 2019); and a ray from a drawing outward is followed exactly, wall by wall, to its last unbounded cell, with the top confidence printed at each wall and at 10 and 100 times the last wall's distance (Hein, Andriushchenko and Bitterwolf, CVPR 2019).

Slices up to dimension 3: a 3-flat through four inputs is cut exactly into convex polyhedra with the same certificate, unique patterns, volumes summing to the cube within 1e-9 relative and a printed count, and a test shows that the 3-flat's cells met by the plate's plane are the plate's cells.

The census reproduces a published result: over at least 100 planes through MNIST test digits, for the shipped network and for networks of the same total neuron count at depths 1 to 4 trained by the committed script, the page plots cells per unit area against the number of neurons and the depth, quotes the growth Hanin and Rolnick (ICML 2019) predict for a 2D slice with its theorem or figure number, and the measured counts follow it within a tolerance committed before the counts were made (a census that only states that it misses does not hold this rung); the counts and the script are committed.

Exact in exact arithmetic: a second implementation in rational arithmetic (BigInt fractions, each weight read as its exact binary value) recomputes the mosaic of at least 3 planes of the shipped network and matches every cell's activation pattern and vertex count, in a node test.

Checked against an independent tool: SplineCam (Humayun et al., CVPR 2023), or another published exact-region tool, run offline on the shipped network and at least 3 of the page's planes, gives the same cell count and patterns; the comparison, the tool's version and the date are committed and linked from the page.

Reference grade: certified exact slices of dimension 1 to 3 through any inputs, for every network the page holds (shipped, hardened, the visitor's lineage, the dial's), compute in a worker in under 100 ms per plane at 1440 px on the stated machine with rungs 4 to 9 passing, and at least 5 independent pages (courses, papers or articles owned by neither Luis nor the builders) cite the lab for exact linear regions, each verified by the rater at its URL.

Rung 2: plate.js run() clips the step from the drawing to its corner to each convex cell (Cyrus and Beck) and the title block prints Walls crossed. Rung 3: split.js mosaic() subdivides the square neuron by neuron through both hidden layers on the plane that plate.js frameAlong() lays through the drawing, its template corner and a third digit, and the title block prints the count with 'exact' (329 on the example 4 in the drives); no grid is on that path. Rung 4 fails: folded.js computes certify() into S.plate.certFailures and writes it only to document.body.dataset.cert, so the page never prints it; engine.test.mjs sections 5 and 6b check the formula, the areas, unique patterns and the certificate on random planes of random networks. Rung 5 would also fail: the visitor does not choose the three drawings (the third is the first example of the rival class, folded.js line 285), and there is no census and no ray.

axes.name: The corner's truth against the network
axes.metric: Agreement of the template with central finite differences (worst error, at most 1e-6); the share of statements on the page about a corner that a forward pass of the exact stepped input backs (target 100%); the threat shapes and input sizes the corner is computed for; and from rung 6 the gap between the one-step corner and stronger searches, in units of full ink.
axes.how_checked: Run the lab's tests; make 10 calls over the examples and 3 drawings of your own, and recompute each claimed reading in node from the stepped input; read the template and step code; set every sentence the page says about a corner beside what the code computes.
ladder: Nothing changes a drawing: no step, corner or attack is computed.
At least a fixed adversarial picture is shown, a perturbed digit stored as an image.
A step is computed in the page: the drawing moved by eps per pixel along a sign pattern, clipped to the pixel range 0 to 1, and the network's answer on the stepped drawing printed.

The template is the cell's map: for the answer a and its rival r, the gradient of z_r minus z_a inside the drawing's cell is computed in closed form from the cell's activation pattern, drawn as a 28 by 28 image in light and dark for its sign, and a node test matches it against central finite differences within 1e-6.

Every statement about what a corner does (it changes the answer, or keeps it) is the result of a forward pass on that exact stepped and clipped input; the page calls the template's sign the first-order corner of the drawing's cell and says a step can leave the cell; and the smallest step along that sign that flips the answer is printed with its unit and the search's resolution, and a node test over at least 20 drawings finds, by a scan of the same range at that resolution, no flipping step below the printed one (a bisection alone assumes the answer flips once along the ray).

Fiction made real (fs-f4, fs-f6, fs-f13, fs-f14): during the step the template shown is replaced at each wall crossed by the template of the cell entered, and a test checks each replacement against the closed form for that cell; the answer flips at the crossing the page marks, checked by a forward pass on each side; the visitor chooses the threat shape (the cube, the cross-polytope and the sphere, each at a radius the page states), each with its worst first-order direction computed (the template's sign for the cube, its single largest pixel for the cross-polytope, the normalised template for the sphere), each shape's first wall found exactly along its own direction with its distance printed, and drawn on a plane laid through the drawing and that direction (the three directions do not share one plane); and the dial runs the same network family trained on 16, 64, 256 and 784 pixels, printing for each the median smallest flipping step over its test digits.

Stronger than one step: projected gradient descent inside the cube (Madry et al., ICLR 2018), its step count and step size stated, runs beside the one-step corner, and over the examples and the visitor's drawings the page prints how many it flips that the one-step corner does not.

The linear account measured: across the dial's 4 input sizes, over at least 100 test digits each, the median smallest flipping step and the template's L1 norm are printed, and a test asserts that the step falls as the size grows, the relation Goodfellow, Shlens and Szegedy (ICLR 2015) give for a linear model (a change of eps per input moves the score by eps times the L1 norm of the weights).

The true worst corner on a small network: on the 16-pixel dial network, the maximum of z_r minus z_a over the whole cube is found exactly (by enumerating the cells the cube meets, or by a mixed-integer program), and for at least 20 drawings the page prints how far the template's corner falls below it.

A universal corner: one sign pattern computed in the page from the templates of many drawings (universal perturbations, Moosavi-Dezfooli et al., CVPR 2017) is applied at the page's eps to at least 1,000 test digits, and the share whose answer it changes is printed for the shipped and the hardened network.

Reference grade: a committed suite of at least 1,000 random drawings, eps values and threat shapes finds no mismatch between any corner claim the page makes and a forward pass or an exact search, on every network the page holds, and at least 5 independent pages cite the lab for adversarial corners, each verified by the rater at its URL.

G0.evidence: Read at 9942268 (not live). Rung 2: call.js stepTo() moves every pixel by eps 0.1 and clips to 0 and 1, and candidates() reads each stepped input. Rung 3: mlp.js template() carries W_L[a] minus W_L[b] back through the cell's masks, folded.js paintSigned() draws it at 28 by 28, and engine.test.mjs section 2 matches it to central differences within 1e-6 (absolute, on synthetic networks). Rung 4 fails on its last clause: every 'read as' comes from argmax(forward()) on the stepped input, and the template note says the sign is the corner that changes the score most 'to first order; a step can cross walls', but call.js smallestFlip() bisects on 0 to 0.5 to a resolution of 0.5/4096 and the ledger prints its step ('Smallest step that changes it, in full ink') with no resolution.

axes.name: Hardening measured against published results
axes.metric: The rise of the drawing's cell template's cosine with the mean rival digit minus the mean answer digit, against a control run on clean digits only (the kill test's measure); clean accuracy and accuracy under the fast gradient sign step on a held set, before and after; the smallest flipping step before and after, in full ink; and from rung 7 each figure's distance from the published value it is set beside.
axes.how_checked: Press Harden on 3 drawings and read the numbers; read the worker and its objective; run the lab's tests; from rung 7 run the committed offline scripts and open each cited paper at the table or section the page names.
ladder: The network never changes on the page.
At least a hardened state is shown, for example by swapping in a second precomputed network file.
A copy of the network trains in the page: gradient steps on digits in the visitor's tab, with the step count shown while it runs.

Adversarial training in the tab: each step trains on the fast gradient sign corners of its batch with the objective of Goodfellow, Shlens and Szegedy (ICLR 2015, section 6), its weight alpha and its eps stated in the code, in a worker so the page keeps responding, and seeded so the same drawings give the same hardened network.

Measured before and after: after each hardening the page prints, for the drawing on the pad, the smallest flipping step before and after (the flip ledger row), and the network's clean accuracy and its accuracy under the fast gradient sign step at the page's eps, each before and after, on a held set of at least 1,000 MNIST test digits that hardening did not use.

Fiction made real (fs-f7, fs-f8, fs-f9): hardening trains on the visitor's own corners mixed with the shipped digits for a few hundred steps in the background; the mosaic of the current plane is redrawn at least every 50 steps while it trains, so the walls are seen to move; the template after hardening is measured by its cosine with the mean rival digit minus the mean answer digit, printed before and after beside a control run of the same steps on clean digits only, with the rise over the control printed, and over the rater's 3 hardened drawings the mean rise over the control is at least 0.05 (the kill test's condition A; a rise printed at or below it shows the template did not turn toward strokes, fs-f8); and the flip ledger keeps one row per drawing hardened, with its smallest flipping step before and after.

The cost of defence (Tsipras et al., ICLR 2019): the visitor's earlier drawings that the hardened network now reads differently are listed with both readings, and the change in clean accuracy on the held set is printed beside the change in robust accuracy, each with its sign.

Set beside Goodfellow, Shlens and Szegedy (ICLR 2015, section 6): a committed offline run of the page's adversarial training on the 60,000 MNIST training digits reports the error on fast gradient sign examples at the paper's eps, before and after, and the page prints both beside the values the paper reports for its own network, naming the difference in architecture.

Set beside Madry et al. (ICLR 2018): a committed offline run of projected-gradient adversarial training at eps 0.3 reports accuracy under that attack on the 10,000 MNIST test digits, printed beside the paper's MNIST value with its table number.

Robust templates across every pair: for the shipped and the hardened network, the mean cosine of the cell template with the class-mean difference is computed for all 45 digit pairs over at least 100 drawings each and drawn as a 10 by 10 matrix, testing on the whole set Tsipras et al.'s (ICLR 2019) observation that robust models' input gradients align with perceptible features.

Reference grade: the in-tab hardening and the committed offline runs agree (the in-tab rise of rung 5 within a stated tolerance of the offline run on the same data and seed), every hardening figure on the page carries its seed, data, step count and source, and at least 5 independent pages cite the lab for adversarial training, each verified by the rater at its URL.

G0.evidence: Read at 9942268 (not live). Rungs 2 and 3: harden.worker.js trains a copy in a module worker with Adam on 0.5 CE(x) + 0.5 CE(fgsm(x)) at the page's eps (Goodfellow, Shlens and Szegedy 2015, alpha 0.5, in its header and mlp.js), posts the weights every 50 steps (the note reads 'Step n of 300'), and is seeded by fnv1a of the drawing. Rung 4 fails: the ledger row before and after is printed (0.042 and over 0.5 on the example 4 in the drives), but no clean or robust accuracy on a held set is computed or printed. Rung 5 would also fail on the control run and the template's cosine, which exist only in the kill test.

axes.name: The visitor's calls and their record
axes.metric: The share of calls whose key the engine computed before the reveal (target 100%); the best share of counted calls any fixed strategy wins (target at most 60%); what of the visitor's work survives a reload and a later visit; and what leaves the page by export and by URL.
axes.how_checked: Make at least 10 calls on examples and on drawings of your own, reload, and compare the tally and the record; use the privacy page's export and erase; run the committed strategy script over the item generator; open a call's URL in a fresh profile.
ladder: Nothing the visitor does is scored or kept.
At least one call: before a step the visitor picks one of several corners, and the page then shows which changed the answer.

The call is keyed by the engine: every candidate is stepped and read by a forward pass before the reveal, a call is right when its corner changes the answer, a call where no corner changes it is voided in words and not counted, and the tally of right of counted calls is computed from the calls.

Kept across reloads: the calls (the pick, its key, its verdict, the time and the mode), the visitor's drawings as 28 by 28 grids and the flip ledger rows come back after a reload, and the privacy page's export contains them and its erase removes them, both driven.

No fixed strategy wins: a committed script over the call's item generator, on the shipped and on the hardened network, shows that always picking one candidate kind or one position is right in at most 60% of counted calls, and no candidate's label before the call names the key.

Fiction made real (fs-f9, fs-f18): the record's share of the flip ledger (its rows, which hardening-measured rung 5 computes) is kept across visits, one row per hardening in the order made, each tied to the lineage step that produced it; the visitor's hardened network is kept across visits as a lineage, with the drawings and corners that made it; a reference network that never sees the visitor is kept beside it; and a corner from an earlier visit can be replayed on today's network and on the reference, both readings shown.
A call round-trips through a URL: the drawing, eps, the network state and the candidates reopen in a fresh profile with the same plate, the same candidates and the same verdict.

The record leaves as data: it downloads as JSON with a documented schema (a version, every unit named, eps in full ink), and a downloaded hardened network loads back into the page and gives the same answers on the visitor's drawings.

Calibration from the record: the visitor's hit rate is shown by corner kind, by eps and by network, each with a Wilson 95% interval (Wilson, JASA 1927), beside the rate a fixed strategy would score on the same items.

Adaptive items: the next call's eps is set from the visitor's record by a transformed up-down rule (two right steps down, one wrong steps up, which tracks 70.7% right; Levitt, JASA 1971), and the page shows the eps the visitor's calls converge to.

Reference grade: an exported record replays in a fresh profile to the same verdicts, tallies, ledger rows and lineage weights, bit for bit, in a committed test, its schema is used unchanged by a second lab's scored act, and at least 5 independent pages cite the lab's flip-calling game or its record of calls, each verified by the rater at its URL.

G0.evidence: Read at 9942268 (not live). Rungs 1 and 2: call.js candidates() steps and reads all three corners before the pick, verdict() counts a call only when some corner changes the answer, the void is said in words ('This call is not counted.'), and record.js tallyOf() computes the tally from the kept calls. Rung 3 is not shown, so taken lower: keep.js writes calls, actions, drawings and ledger rows through Labs OS (lab 'dimensional') and the drives read them back after a reload, but the privacy page's export and erase of that record were driven neither by this reading nor by the pre-grade of c268995. Rung 4 would fail: the kill test measured the template corner at eps 0.1 moving 96 of 98 test 4s off 4 on the baseline network (kill_test RESULT.md), and the corners are drawn as pictures before the call, so picking the structured one wins near that share; no strategy script exists.

axes.name: The plate and the central scene
axes.metric: Count of the central scene's parts drawn from computed state (the answer on the 9-simplex, the plate, the run, the template, the 784-hairline cube, the hardening redraw, the fold, the unfold, the smooth scene); count of linked views; and the share of marks that encode a computed value (target 100%).
axes.how_checked: Shoot the page at 1440 and 390 px in every state with node tools/labs-wt.mjs shoot and read the frames through the labs-design skill; inspect the plate's SVG or canvas source for marks bound to no computed value; hover, tap and select in each view and note which others answer.
ladder: Nothing is drawn.
At least a static image: a picture of cells or of a digit.
One live view drawn from computed state: the answer, or the cells drawn from the computed mosaic.

The plate and its companions encode values: the cells drawn as hairline polygons on a graticule labelled with its scale in units of full ink, the drawing and its corner marked, the template drawn as a 28 by 28 image in light and dark for its sign, and the answer drawn as a point inside the 9-simplex's projection at the probability-weighted place.

Linked marks: hovering, tapping or focusing a wall names its neuron and layer, tapping a cell lifts its template, the run from the drawing to its corner draws one tick per wall crossed and the tick count equals the walls-crossed figure, and gold falls only on what fired.

Fiction made real (fs-f2, fs-f3, fs-f4, fs-f5, fs-f6, fs-f11, fs-f12, fs-f19): the 784-cube is drawn as a starburst of 784 hairlines, one toward each pixel; the step animates the drawing changing by a shade per pixel while the dot crosses the walls one at a time and the template swaps at each crossing; during hardening the walls move continuously (fs-f7, and Luis's rule of 2026-11-21 that transitions are organic, not a disappearing and appearing): between two posted weight sets the plate draws the exact mosaic of weights interpolated between them, so every frame is a true mosaic, and a fading trail of earlier places may stay behind as persistence (BAR_L1.md); the fold is drawn in 3D, the plane folding along the first layer's walls with the count climbing; the unfold player shows the plane's image after each hidden layer of a network of at least 4 hidden layers, projected to 3D, and steps it back layer by layer to the flat input plane and its exact cells; and the smooth-activation scene draws its walls as bands; the scene reveals by ignition (the drawing, the answer, the first layer's walls, the second layer's, then the run) before its material moves (atlas graphics.5.4); each from computed state, and under reduced motion each as its finished frame.
Several linked views share one selection: selecting a cell on the plate lights its point on the simplex, its template and its pixels on the starburst, and selecting in any of those lights the plate.

Choreography, timed and true: the ignition finishes in under 4 s and is skippable, and 10 frames sampled from a recording of the step and 10 from a recording of hardening each match the engine's state at that moment (the drawing at that fraction of the step, the exact mosaic of those interpolated weights), checked in node.
Exact at any zoom: zooming the plate up to 1,000 times recomputes the cells of the zoomed square, walls stay one device pixel wide, cells too small for the wider view appear, and the count updates.
A 3-flat view: the cells of a 3D slice through four drawings are drawn as convex polyhedra, rotatable and cut by a movable plane, and the cut shows the same cells as the plate computed on that plane.

Reference grade: every view of the scene, at 390 to 2560 px, is drawn from computed state with no region tagged illustrative, and at least 5 independent pages use the lab's plates to explain linear regions or adversarial corners, each verified by the rater at its URL.

G0.evidence: Read at 9942268 (not live). Rung 2: folded.js drawPlate() draws the computed mosaic's polygons, drawSimplex() the softmax point and paintSigned() the template. Rung 3 fails: the plate's 10 by 10 graticule and its 50 minor ticks carry no scale or label (drawPlate). Above the break: the run and one tick per crossing are drawn from plate.js run(), gold only when the template's corner changed the answer (the 'quiet' class otherwise); there is no wall hover, no cell tap and no starburst, and the run is drawn whole with no sweep.

axes.name: The Machine's material
axes.metric: Defects against the Machine's material: gold marks outside what fired (target 0, from a grep of the lab's styles and scripts for the --accretion family and its hex values); controls not from the shared kit; text under 12 px or fainter than --text-dim; the anti_tells count; overlaps at 390 and 1440 px; and from rung 5 the bar sheet's parts and states present. The world is the road's default, Inside the Machine, which Luis has not decided (asked 2026-11-19): if he places the lab in another world, rungs 5 to 7 and 10 are rewritten for that world's material before the next grade (LABS_LEVELS.md rule 3), and rungs 0 to 4, 8 and 9, which name no world, stand.
axes.how_checked: Shoot every state at 390x844 and 1440x900 and read the frames through the labs-design skill; grep the lab's CSS and scripts for accretion and its hex values and place each hit; read computed font sizes and colours in DevTools; run node tools/anti_tells.mjs scan on the lab's files; measure the gold share of a resting screenshot.
ladder: Browser defaults: unstyled text and controls.
At least a dark ground and a styled canvas.

The site's tokens: colours only from tokens.css, data and interface text in IBM Plex Mono through tokens.css's font tokens (var(--font-mono) and its siblings, never the family named in the lab's styles), prose in Fraunces named in one place (tokens.css declares no Fraunces token), fonts loaded without blocking first paint, and no browser-default control chrome.

Gold only for what fired, and one control language: every gold mark sits on a computed answer, a run made, a corner that changed the answer or a right call, and nothing else is gold (a zero tally, an unpicked or unchanged corner, the graticule and the walls included), and every button and toggle uses the shared controls of labs/assets/css/controls.css.

Legible and clean: no text under 12 px at 390 or 1440 px, no text a visitor must read fainter than --text-dim, labels over the plate set in HTML so they keep their size at 390 px, no overlap or clipped panel at 390x844 or 1440x900, and node tools/anti_tells.mjs scan reports 0 on the lab's files.

Fiction made real in the Machine's material: the plate reads as an oscilloscope screen (a graticule with minor ticks on both axes, walls as hairlines at half strength); the run sweeps over about half a second and leaves a trigger tick at each wall; cells the run passed keep a persistence fill of at most 13% opacity (BAR_L1.md's effects budget) that decays over seconds; walls migrating during hardening are drawn as persistence; gold covers under 1% of a resting screenshot; the lab differs from the other worlds on at least 4 of geometry, texture, ornament, motion and ink tint; and every part of the lab's level-1 bar sheet is present in each of its listed states, shot at 390 and 1440 px.

Motion grammar: the sweep, the persistence decay and the wall migration use the site's easing and duration tokens, and under reduced motion each is replaced by its finished frame (the run whole with its ticks, the hardened mosaic with no migration).

Phosphor precision: each trigger tick sits within 0.5 px of its computed crossing at 390 and 1440 px, persistence decays by one exponential whose time constant is a named constant, and hairlines stay one device pixel wide at every zoom.
A style lint, one command, fails on any colour, font family or font size in the lab's styles and scripts that tokens.css does not declare, and it passes.
At 390, 768, 1024, 1440 and 2560 px, in every state: no overlap or clipped panel, and every text at least 4.5:1 against what is behind it, sampled with a contrast tool.
The Machine's material as shared kit: the graticule, the trigger ticks, the sweep and the persistence are lifted into labs/assets and used unchanged by at least one other lab of Inside the Machine.

axes.name: The visitor's hand on the network
axes.metric: Count of the visitor's verbs on the network (draw, choose drawings, call, harden, select a wall or a cell, drag the drawing's point, drag a wall, scrub a player), each checked by mouse, by touch at 390 px and by keyboard; the pad's reading accuracy on digits drawn by people; and whether state restores from a link.
axes.how_checked: Perform each verb by mouse, by touch in DevTools emulation at 390 px and by keyboard; run the pointer probe drive and the pad's node test; read the committed log of people's drawings; open a copied URL in a fresh profile.
ladder: Nothing to touch.
At least presets: example digits choose what the network reads.

A pad: the visitor draws by mouse or touch, the drawing is reduced as MNIST's were (cropped to its ink, the longer side scaled to 20 px with anti-aliasing, the centre of mass placed at the middle of 28 by 28), and the answer updates while the stroke is drawn.

The pad reads what it is given: a node test reduces at least 100 MNIST test digits over all 10 classes, each drawn large on the pad at 4 places and scales, and reads at least 97% as their label, and a drive drawing 20 digits through pointer events reads at least 18 as written at 1440 and at 390 px.

Direct manipulation: the visitor chooses the drawings that lay the plane, selects a wall or a cell by pointer and by keyboard focus, and drags the drawing's point across the plate while the pad shows the input at that point of the plane and the answer updates, the inverse of drawing.

Fiction made real (fs-f1, fs-f10): the network reads people's drawings, at least 90% of at least 100 digits drawn on the page by at least 5 people who did not build it, with the log committed; walls by hand runs, two clouds of points in a plane and an empty network, each first-layer neuron a wall the visitor drags, the second layer's walls drawn bending where they meet the first's, with the count and the training loss updating; and every verb of the scene (draw, choose, call, harden, select, drag the point, drag a wall, scrub the fold and the unfold player) works by mouse, by touch at 390 px and by keyboard, drawing included through a keyboard pen.
State in the URL: the drawings, eps, the plane and the network state (shipped, or hardened with its seed) round-trip through a link opened in a fresh profile.
